recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future changes to these code definitions are needed, route them through THO/UTG rather than reintroducing a core CodeSystem file unless FHIR core ownership changes.
issue_request: FHIR-15784 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for STU3. It asked that Consent Action sibling codes be made mutually exclusive or arranged in a proper hierarchy, and resolved to revise definitions for collect, access, use, disclose, and correct until V3 harmonization was complete.
initial_application: Commit 7c8a912aeb6ff6bb22b167c37089bf18b5005a1c applied GF#15784 by changing source/consent/codesystem-consent-action.xml definitions for the five codes. The changed definitions appear in generated R4 terminology history. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 later removed that core CodeSystem source during the UTG/THO terminology migration.
additional_context: Current core source has Consent active in source/fhir.ini, binds Consent.provision.action to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/consent-action, and defines that value set as all codes from http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/consentaction. The current published THO CodeSystem preserves the FHIR-15784 definitions. Later FHIR-48780 only promoted Consent terminology metadata to active/non-experimental, and FHIR-15796 was a no-change request to add a none code.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source edit is needed because the build-scope core ValueSet correctly delegates to the external THO CodeSystem and the external definitions already match the FHIR-15784 resolution.

related_jiras.note: Promoted valueset-consent-action to active/non-experimental for R6 without changing the action definitions.
Requested adding a none code to Consent Action Codes but was Resolved - No Change, so it does not require code additions here.
